title: Why You'd Never Want To Meet A Blue Whale
description: Facts: blue whale up to ~30 m, heart ~180 kg (est.), krill up to ~4 t/day; great white up to ~6 m; sperm whale dives >2,000 m; Challenger Deep ~10,900 m; orcas prey on great whites. All animal art drawn procedurally, nothing to credit.

beats.text: Picture this. You're floating in open water, and something enormous glides past.
A blue whale reaches thirty metres. That is longer than two city buses, and the biggest animal ever known.
Its heart alone weighs about one hundred and eighty kilograms.
Yet it eats animals the size of your finger. Krill. Up to four tonnes a day.
Most people think the ocean's biggest hunter is a shark. That is the myth.

scene.text: The biggest hunter is a *shark*. Or is it?

beats.text: A great white reaches about six metres, and can sprint at around fifty kilometres an hour.
Next to the giants, it is small. A sperm whale is sixteen metres. An orca is around eight.
And a sperm whale will dive past two thousand metres, far below where sunlight reaches, to hunt in total darkness.
The deepest point on Earth, the Mariana Trench, is nearly eleven thousand metres down. No whale goes there.
So who really rules? The orca. Pods of orcas have been filmed hunting great whites.
Three hunters. One rule. In open water, you are never at the top.
